newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products all knocked lower, except fuel oil.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products all knocked lower, except fuel oil.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were all easier taking a lead from easier crude and sharply lower gas oil. Only fuel showed any steadiness.
Fuel oil prices were steady with little business to move numbers in any direction. But traders were bearish about post-Easter trade.
"I still see the Mediterranean as marginally long," said one broker.
Reports that transatlantic supplies of low sulphur fuel might flow east were accepted by some but discounted by others, who thought the arbitrage too tight.

High and low sulphur prices are firmer than in northern Europe, but buying demand is light, with some interest soaked up by the three cargo trades done on a floating price basis out of a major's Italian refinery earlier this week.
Russian straight-run cargoes were heard to be finding buyers but supplies may back up later in April, traders said.
Moving naphtha to the thirsty Asian market was becoming harder with strong freight rates acting as a further discouragement to the easing of Asian prices.
Activity was slow on Thursday with most trading houses looking to the Easter week-end rather than trading cargoes.

Gas oil was looking a touch bearish after heavy screen losses and easier premiums in the north. Traders said the draw from Asia was now looking a touch less attractive although talk was still centred on this.
Russians were pegged around fob high quotes +$1.50, a drop of 50 cents or so while Italian grade 0.2 percent was pegged around cif high quotes +$2.
Diesel was weakened as the market heads towards summer spec in two weeks time dropping $2-3 a tonne.
